newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Conservatives replace drink-drive leader.
newsitem.headline: Danish Conservatives replace drink-drive leader.

text.p: Denmark's opposition Conservative Party on Monday named Per Stig Moeller as party leader to replace Hans Engell, who quit on Friday after a car accident in which his blood-alcohol level was over the legal limit.
Moeller, 54, environmental minister from 1990-93 and the author of literary and philosophical works, represents the left wing of the Danish Conservative Party.
Moeller said he would maintain the Conservatives' traditional alliance with the Liberal Party in opposition to the ruling Social Democrats.
"There can be no doubt that we are aiming for the formation of a Conservative-Liberal government with the support of centre parties," Moeller told a news conference.
Engell, 48, remains leader of the party's parliamentary group, a largely administrative post.
He resigned last Friday, one day after his car veered off a motorway north of the capital and hit a lamp post.
Engell was unhurt and reported the accident to police. A blood test showed he had a blood alcohol content of 1.37, above the legal limit of 0.8 units of alcohol per thousand units of blood.

Local authority polls are due in Denmark in November this year, and general elections by September 1998. Opinion polls tip a Liberal-Conservative alliance as likely to oust the incumbent Social Democrat-led coalition.
The latest polls show Engell's accident and the Conservatives' leadership change have not damaged the ratings of the rightist Liberal-Conservative bloc.
A Conservative-Liberal coalition under Conservative Prime Minister Poul Schlueter ruled Denmark from 1982 to 1993, when it was ousted by a Social Democrat-led centre-left coalition.
